analysis: Both changed files are documentation only; no executable code, configuration, or trust-boundary behavior changes in the supplied evidence. docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date bump, a note that inline GLM video input may be constant or variable frame rate (line 52 in the patch excerpt, not in the numbered units), and a new path-table row at head line 1578 for ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json (DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE, mode 0600). That row describes managed GLM load hashes bound to file identities and reused for startup registration. It is relevant to A-004, T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution and weight-hash integrity). The documented design binds hashes to file identities, but the VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift implementation was not supplied, so I cannot confirm that a cached hash is invalidated when weights are modified (size, mtime, inode/identity binding, tamper handling of a user-writable 0600 file). A reused cached hash could let an operator who swaps weights after verification keep advertising the stale hash at registration. That depends on code outside this PR's visible evidence, so it is recorded as an unverified contract rather than a finding. docs/provider/direct-mode.md: date bump and a note that a local GLM qualification load performs its own per-file SHA-256 verification as the artifact hash, with no separate weight-hash passes (GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256). This is a standalone/local qualification path that the doc says is never advertised to the coordinator, so it does not affect the coordinator trust model. The remaining direct-mode text is unchanged. Next pass should confirm the implementation of VerifiedWeightHashStore (file-identity binding, freshness, and fail-closed behavior) against T-012/T-027 if source for it is in the PR.
